leftEvidence.title: Son of David cries enter Jerusalem and the Temple

points.label: Action and response
points.left: Jesus rides into Jerusalem, crowds use royal psalm language, the city asks who he is, Temple commerce is overturned, blind and lame people are healed, and children cry “Hosanna to the son of David.”.
points.right: Jesus asks how scribes say the Christ is David’s son, cites David speaking by the Holy Spirit, and asks how the figure David calls Lord is his son.

points.label: Evidence boundary
points.left: The source places Davidic acclaim moves from road to Temple and provokes priestly indignation inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.
points.right: The source places the crowd’s glad hearing does not answer the relation Jesus asks about inside this David setting without explaining every motive, transition, or later consequence.

payload.posture: Matthew 21:1–17 and Mark 12:35–37 are distinct approved David Scenes in the authored “Gospel and Apostolic Memory” movement; holding them together exposes what continues and what changes without collapsing their sources.

rightEvidence.title: Mark preserves the Davidic lordship question

payload.tension: Matthew 21:1–17 foregrounds Davidic acclaim moves from road to Temple and provokes priestly indignation; Mark 12:35–37 foregrounds the crowd’s glad hearing does not answer the relation Jesus asks about. Their sequence does not by itself explain every change between them.
